name: To Make an Orange Pudding
description: Historical recipe from The Virginia Housewife; Or, Methodical Cook (1824). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Put two oranges and two lemons into five quarts of water
Boil them till the rinds are quite tender
Take them out, and when cold, slice them thin, and pick out the seeds
Put a pound of loaf sugar into a pint of water
When it boils, slice into it twelve pippins pared and cored
Lay in the lemons and oranges, stew them tender
Cover the dish with puff paste, lay the fruit in carefully, in alternate layers
Pour on the syrup, put some slips of paste across, and bake it

source.author: Mary Randolph
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put two oranges and two lemons into five quarts of water
2. Boil them till the rinds are quite tender
3. Take them out, and when cold, slice them thin, and pick out the seeds
4. Put a pound of loaf sugar into a pint of water
5. When it boils, slice into it twelve pippins pared and cored
6. Lay in the lemons and oranges, stew them tender
7. Cover the dish with puff paste, lay the fruit in carefully, in alternate layers
8. Pour on the syrup, put some slips of paste across, and bake it
